isl.source: sign.mt (closest equivalent: hello; sign.mt has no sign for "namaste")

notes: sign.mt translates word by word. A 200 answer can be synthetic fingerspelling (one hand tracked in every frame, the other in none); those are rejected and left to the app's own fingerspelling. ISL answers 500 instead of spelling.
sign.mt only matches base forms through its gloss index, so inflected words ("comprends", "buenos días") are often spelled even when the base word has a sign.
Multi-token word-list items are kept only if every token has its own real sign (ISL silently drops unknown tokens).
Idle frames (no hand in view) at the start and end are trimmed before conversion, keeping ~0.12 s margin.
ISL is queried in English: sign.mt splits Devanagari at vowel signs, so Hindi queries only return single-letter matches or "No poses found".

A phrase animation is kept unless a content word was dropped (ISL has no fingerspelling, so unknown words vanish) or, for LSF, a content word was fingerspelled with sign.mt's ASL letters. Function words may be dropped or spelled.
